name: Execute public market orders through brokers and venues
summary: The central trading desk takes orders that portfolio managers and the balancing team have placed and cleared through pre-trade compliance, and executes them in global equity, government bond, FX and listed derivative markets. Traders choose between broker algorithms, negotiated high-touch orders, program trades for rebalancing baskets and competing dealer quotes, then watch orders until they are filled, carried over or cancelled. Fills are checked against broker summaries and passed to trade support for booking, and the next day transaction cost analysis flags expensive orders for explanation and review. Work is slowed by time zones, by large orders that must be worked over hours or days to limit market impact, and by fill discrepancies and the occasional trade error.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager that runs one global fund with mostly internal teams and a central trading desk for all public assets except credit.
baseline.notes: Order volume follows the organisation file estimate of about 25,000 orders a month (about 1,200 a trading day). The desk works from Toronto with traders in London and Hong Kong. Credit trades are executed by Credit Investments and are outside this workflow.

trigger: An order that has passed pre-trade compliance and been accepted by a trader appears on the central desk's execution blotter.
end_state: The order is fully executed or its residual cancelled, the execution report has gone to booking, and the next-day cost review is closed; or the portfolio manager has withdrawn the order.

volume.seasonality: Higher in volatile markets (March 2020), at quarter-ends and index rebalancing dates, and when the Balancing Portfolio rebalances; lower in late December and summer.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate (driver public_orders), about 1,200 orders a trading day; the fund does not publish trade counts.

26 traders in the organisation file also accept and plan orders in order capture and help with funding trades; about 19 FTE assumed on execution, close to the 22 FTE implied by hands-on time. Loaded cost from the organisation file, far above the Job Bank NOC 11103 Toronto median of C$47.18 an hour because incentive pay is large at this employer.
Four desk heads split between supervising execution, escalations and errors, broker reviews and management.
Periodic trade oversight meetings only.
Represents all order originators (CMF, AE, TFM balancing) answering trader queries; small share of their time.

systems.name: Order and execution management system with pre-trade compliance rules
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse

steps.name: Accepted order appears on the execution blotter
steps.description: After pre-trade compliance and trader acceptance in order capture, the order and execution management system places the order on the central desk's blotter in the queue for its asset class and region (equities, rates, FX, listed derivatives) and alerts the assigned trader. No one touches the order at this point.
inputs: staged trade order with compliance pass

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Orders start upstream in the OMS and pass compliance before reaching the desk (factset_desk); FCT executes all public assets except credit for all teams (ar21).

steps.name: Check market conditions and confirm execution approach
steps.description: The trader opens the order ticket, compares the size with average daily volume, spread and volatility on Bloomberg and in the EMS, re-reads the portfolio manager's urgency, limit and benchmark instructions and confirms the approach planned at acceptance. Orders for markets that are closed are parked, and orders whose instructions no longer fit the market go back to the portfolio manager.

error.defect_description: Instruction misread (side, limit or benchmark) and carried into the execution.

control.basis: Investment policy and trade management policy: portfolio managers decide trades and only the central desk sends orders to brokers through the OMS/EMS

next.condition: local market not yet open (pre-open Toronto orders, Asia-Pacific and European orders)
instruction unclear, limit stale or size too large for current liquidity

evidence.note: Order, security and market inputs drive strategy choice (cfa_tse). Shares are author estimates for a desk trading 64 countries from Toronto, London and Hong Kong.

steps.name: Park order until the local market opens or hand it to the regional desk
steps.description: Orders for markets that are closed wait in the OMS with a start time, or are passed in the blotter to the Hong Kong or London traders who work those time zones. Pre-open Toronto and New York orders, many generated by overnight rebalancing, wait for the opening auction.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Follow-the-sun desks in Toronto, London and Hong Kong are implied by the nine offices in the organisation file; wait ranges cover a pre-open wait of minutes to an overnight wait for Asia-Pacific orders.

steps.name: Query the order with the portfolio manager
steps.description: The trader messages or calls the portfolio manager or balancing team to explain the issue (limit away from the market, order above a set share of daily volume, a trading halt or news) and proposes options such as a wider limit, a longer horizon or a smaller size.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate; return of orders to the portfolio manager is named in the order capture process description.

steps.name: Portfolio manager amends, confirms or withdraws the order
steps.description: The portfolio manager decides whether to keep the order as is, change the limit, size or horizon in the OMS (which re-runs the compliance check upstream) or withdraw it, and tells the trader in chat.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: order confirmed or amended within existing compliance pass
order re-entered with new terms and returns to the blotter

evidence.note: Author estimate. The portfolio manager role stands in for all order originators (CMF, AE, TFM balancing).

steps.name: Choose execution channel for the order
steps.description: The trader decides between a broker algorithm or direct market access, a negotiated high-touch order with a broker's sales trader, a program trade for a basket, or a request for quotes to dealers for FX, government bonds and some derivatives. Very large or sensitive orders need the head of desk's agreement on the strategy first.

error.defect_description: Channel or urgency poorly matched to liquidity, raising market impact.

next.condition: liquid listed equity, ETF or futures order: algorithm or direct market access
illiquid or large equity order: negotiated with a broker
order is part of a rebalancing basket: program trade
FX, government bond or OTC-quoted order: request for quotes
order above the desk's size or sensitivity threshold

evidence.note: Coalition Greenwich: high-touch fell to 44% and algorithm/DMA/smart routing rose to 35% of U.S. institutional equity volume in the year to Q1 2021 (greenwich_ht). Shares by order count for this multi-asset desk are author estimates: low-touch orders are smaller and more numerous than high-touch orders.

steps.name: Head of desk agrees strategy for a large or sensitive order
steps.description: The director reviews the pre-trade cost estimate, the order's share of daily volume and information-leakage risk, and agrees the broker shortlist, horizon and whether to seek a block or capital commitment.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Desk trading procedures: senior sign-off on execution strategy for orders above size or liquidity thresholds

next.condition: work with a broker for block liquidity
work through an algorithm over a longer horizon

evidence.note: Author estimate of common desk practice; the CFA trade governance reading calls for factors that set the execution approach to be written in policy (cfa_tse).

steps.name: Select broker algorithm and route the order
steps.description: The trader picks an approved broker and algorithm (VWAP, implementation shortfall, percent of volume, close or a dark aggregator), sets limit, participation and start and end times in the EMS and sends the order to the broker over FIX.

error.defect_description: Wrong algorithm parameter (limit, participation, end time) entered.

control.basis: Approved broker list: only brokers approved through counterparty credit review and the desk's broker review may receive orders

evidence.note: Algorithm classes from cfa_tse; parent orders sent to broker algorithms with start and end times and participation limits (nber_algo).

steps.name: Negotiate the order with a broker's sales trader
steps.description: The trader calls or chats with an approved broker's sales trader on a recorded line, describes the order without revealing more than needed, asks for natural block interest or a capital commitment, agrees the commission rate and hands over the order.

error.defect_description: Verbal miscommunication of size, limit or side.

control.basis: Approved broker list and recorded lines for voice orders under the trade management policy

evidence.note: Traders weigh broker relationships and liquidity insight for larger, less liquid orders (factset_desk); high-touch remains 44% of U.S. institutional equity volume (greenwich_ht).

steps.name: Bid the rebalancing basket as a program trade
steps.description: For a basket from the balancing or currency teams the trader sends anonymised list characteristics (sector, liquidity, beta, value) to three or four program desks, compares risk or agency bids and awards the basket. The work is shared across every order in the basket, so the time per order is small.
outputs: basket awarded to a program desk

error.defect_description: Constituent left out of or duplicated in the basket.

control.basis: Best execution policy: competitive bids for program trades

evidence.note: Author estimate; basket size of 50 to 400 names assumed for balancing trades.

steps.name: Program desk executes the basket
steps.description: A risk bid is filled at once against the agreed benchmark; an agency program is worked by the broker over the day to the agreed benchmark, often the close. The broker returns fills per constituent.
inputs: basket awarded to a program desk

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate: risk bids fill immediately, agency programs run to the close (up to seven hours).

steps.name: Request competing quotes from dealers
steps.description: For FX forwards and spot, government bonds and some derivatives the trader sends a request for quotes to three to five approved dealers on a multi-dealer platform or Bloomberg, compares the prices, executes with the best and keeps the losing quotes as best execution evidence. Large FX orders may instead be worked over time or placed at a benchmark fix.
outputs: executed RFQ trade or working order

error.defect_description: Wrong value date, tenor or amount on an FX or bond trade.

control.basis: Best execution policy requiring competing quotes for OTC trades; FX Global Code execution principles

next.condition: large order worked over time or at a fix

evidence.note: FX Global Code execution principles and block allocation guidance (fxgc). Quote counts and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Broker or algorithm works the order in the market
steps.description: The algorithm or broker slices the parent order into child orders across lit and dark venues according to the chosen strategy until it is complete, reaches its end time or hits its limit. Fills stream back to the EMS.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: The average algorithmic parent order tried to trade US$287,000 over 84 minutes, 4.8% of volume over its duration, across 2.3 million parent orders from 961 institutions (nber_algo). The mode is set above 84 minutes because a pension fund's orders are larger and many run to the close.

steps.name: Monitor the working order and adjust
steps.description: While the order works, the trader watches fills against the arrival price and interval VWAP in the EMS, changes participation or limits when prices move, pauses for news or halts, and switches broker if performance is poor.

error.defect_description: Late reaction to a price move or halt.

next.condition: unusual impact, news or broker problem
order not complete by its end time or the close

evidence.note: Real-time monitoring and benchmark choice (arrival price, VWAP) from factset_desk and cfa_tse; branch shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Escalate unusual market conditions to the head of desk
steps.description: The trader brings the director an order that is moving the price, a broker outage or a news event. The director decides whether to continue, change strategy or broker, or stop and consult the portfolio manager.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Desk escalation procedures in the trade management policy

next.condition: stop and decide on the residual

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Decide on the unfilled residual
steps.description: At the order's end time or the close the trader checks the unfilled quantity, consults the portfolio manager when the residual is material and either carries it to the next session or cancels it and reports a partial fill.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: carry the residual to the next session
cancel the residual and report the partial fill

evidence.note: Author estimate; multi-day working of large orders is common for institutional managers (nber_algo describes parent orders with set durations).

steps.name: Hand the carried order to the next desk or day
steps.description: The trader writes a handover note in the blotter and team chat with the filled quantity, average price, market colour and instructions so that the next regional desk or the same desk next morning can resume the order.

error.defect_description: Handover note omits a limit or instruction change.

evidence.note: Author estimate of follow-the-sun practice across Toronto, London and Hong Kong.

steps.name: Order waits for the next trading session
steps.description: The OMS rolls the order to the next session as a good-till-cancelled order. Over a weekend or holiday the wait is longer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Overnight gap of 10 to 17 hours, up to 65 hours over a weekend.

steps.name: Check fills against the broker's execution summary
steps.description: At completion the trader compares the fills in the EMS with the broker's end-of-day execution summary (quantity, average price, commission rate, broker) and keys any voice fills that did not arrive electronically.

error.defect_description: Manually keyed voice fill has a wrong price or quantity.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: trades authorised and recorded accurately and completely (SOC 1 baseline trading objective)

next.condition: execution does not match the order (side, size or security)

evidence.note: SIFMA AMG baseline objective: trades properly authorised and recorded accurately, completely and timely (sifma_soc). Break shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a fill discrepancy with the broker
steps.description: The trader asks the broker's desk to correct or cancel the wrong fill, checks the corrected execution report in the EMS and notes the fix.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: the discrepancy is a trade error

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Handle a trade error
steps.description: The head of desk confirms the error, decides on the correcting trade, agrees with the broker who bears the cost so that the fund is made whole, informs the portfolio manager and logs the error for operational risk.
outputs: correcting trade and error log entry

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Trade error policy: prompt correction, fund made whole, error logged with operational risk

evidence.note: Trade error handling is a SOC 1 trading area (sifma_soc) and part of a written trade policy (cfa_tse). Time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Release execution report to booking
steps.description: The trader marks the order done and the OMS sends the execution report with average price, quantity, broker and commission to trade support and the book of record for allocation and booking.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: high-touch or program order needs a best execution note
electronic order with automatic audit trail

evidence.note: About 20% of U.S. institutional allocations are made during the trading day and 80% after the close (t1report).

steps.name: Record the best execution rationale
steps.description: The trader adds a note in the EMS on why the broker, venue or dealer was chosen, the competing quotes or bids received and any block or capital commitment, so that the decision can be reviewed later.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Trade management and best execution policy record keeping (CFA Institute Trade Management Guidelines)

evidence.note: Written trade policy covering eligible brokers and monitoring of execution arrangements (cfa_tse).

steps.name: Overnight transaction cost analysis screens the order
steps.description: Overnight the transaction cost analysis tool compares each order's prices with arrival price, interval VWAP and close and flags orders whose cost falls outside set limits for their size and difficulty.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: order flagged as a cost outlier

evidence.note: Implementation shortfall is the standard total cost measure and trade evaluation reviews trader, broker and algorithm (cfa_tse); TCA results feed back into routing (factset_desk). Overnight batch timing and the 7% flag rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Explain the cost outlier
steps.description: The trader opens the order's timeline of fills, market moves and news, and writes a short explanation of why costs were high (news, thin liquidity, poor broker or algorithm performance, or a late start).

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Head of desk reviews outliers
steps.description: The director reviews the outlier list and explanations, decides whether broker or algorithm choices need to change and picks out cases for the periodic trade oversight review.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Best execution monitoring under the trade management policy

next.condition: referred to the trade oversight review

evidence.note: Policy should include a process to monitor execution arrangements (cfa_tse). Weekly review cadence is an author estimate.

steps.name: Trade oversight review of referred orders
steps.description: At the periodic trade oversight meeting the managing director and desk heads go through referred orders, broker scorecards and error logs and record actions such as cutting a broker's allocation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Trade oversight committee recommended by the CFA Institute Trade Management Guidelines

evidence.note: Broker selection and retention and best execution are named control areas (sifma_soc); monthly cadence is an author estimate.

exceptions.name: Order for a closed market
exceptions.description: Pre-open Toronto and New York orders and Asia-Pacific or European orders wait for the local open or are passed to the regional desk.

exceptions.name: Order returned to the portfolio manager
exceptions.description: A stale limit, a size too large for current liquidity or a halt sends the order back; about one in ten of these is withdrawn.

exceptions.name: Residual carried to the next session
exceptions.description: Large or illiquid orders not complete by the close are handed over and resumed the next day, sometimes for several days.

exceptions.name: Fill discrepancy
exceptions.description: A missing, duplicate or mispriced fill is corrected with the broker before release to booking.

exceptions.name: Trade error
exceptions.description: Wrong side, size or security is corrected with a new trade, the fund is made whole and the error is logged.

exceptions.name: Cost outlier
exceptions.description: Next-day TCA flags an expensive order that the trader must explain and the head of desk reviews; a few go to the trade oversight review.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the order reaching the blotter to the close of next-day cost review
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a large institutional multi-asset desk

evidence.note: Most orders are complete on the day they arrive (average algorithmic parent order runs 84 minutes, nber_algo) and the overnight TCA run adds about 16 hours; p90 covers orders carried over several sessions and outlier reviews.

benchmarks.unit: share of volume, year to Q1 2021

evidence.note: 44%, down from 56% in 2012.

benchmarks.unit: share of volume, year to Q1 2021

evidence.note: 35%, up from 29% in 2012.

benchmarks.population: 2.3 million parent orders from 961 institutions, 2012 to 2016

evidence.note: Average parent order US$287,000, 4.8% of volume over its duration.

pain_points.description: Orders arrive in bursts from rebalancing and must wait for local market opens across many time zones, so the desk relies on handovers between Toronto, London and Hong Kong.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the desk's global coverage.

pain_points.description: Large balancing trades must be worked slowly to limit market impact, which lengthens execution and creates residuals to carry over.

evidence.note: Balancing trades in volatile markets (ar21); market impact as one of the largest trading costs (cfa_tse).

pain_points.description: Voice and RFQ executions need manual fill checks and best execution notes, while the order, execution and booking systems were not yet one integrated platform.

evidence.note: The F2021 report describes a multi-year project to build an integrated platform for public market trades across the trading life cycle.

pain_points.description: Cost outliers are only seen the next day, and broker reviews happen on a slow periodic cycle.

evidence.note: Author estimate of common TCA practice in the period.

sources.supports: Toronto Region hourly wages for NOC 11103: low 21.54, median 47.18, high 88.94 (2023-2024)

assumptions: Order capture, pre-trade compliance and the trader's acceptance and plan belong to mkt-order-capture; this workflow starts when the accepted order is on the execution blotter and includes a short re-check at the time of working.
Credit trades are executed by Credit Investments (ci-public-credit-decisions) and are excluded; rates, FX, equity and listed derivative orders are included.

Channel shares by order count (50% algorithm or DMA, 8% high-touch, 14% program, 24% RFQ, 4% large orders needing desk-head sign-off) are author estimates; Coalition Greenwich volume shares for U.S. equities are used only as an anchor.
The portfolio manager role is represented by cmf_principal, standing in for all originators (CMF, Active Equities and TFM balancing staff).

Loaded costs come from the organisation file (total compensation including incentives times 1.25 overhead over 1,950 paid hours); they are far above Job Bank market medians because incentive pay is large at this employer.
The cycle time includes the overnight transaction cost analysis run, so it measures the order's full life on the desk rather than only the time to the last fill.
Trade oversight and broker review meetings are periodic; they enter the workflow only through referred orders, so their fixed meeting time is not counted per order.
